popular.title: Popular Questions
popular.q1_question: What is the biggest festival in Cusco?
popular.q1_answer: Inti Raymi, the Festival of the Sun, is the largest and most famous theatrical reenactment of an ancient Inca ceremony.

popular.q2_answer: June is a particularly busy month for festivals in Cusco, including the famous Inti Raymi and Corpus Christi.

inti-raymi.location_detail: Main events at Qorikancha, Plaza de Armas and Sacsayhuamán.
inti-raymi.description: The ancient Inca festival of the sun, a spectacular theatrical reenactment.
inti-raymi.longDescription: Inti Raymi, the "Festival of the Sun," was the most important religious ceremony of the Inca Empire in honor of the god Inti. Today, it is a massive theatrical representation held every year on June 24 in Cusco. It involves hundreds of actors in vibrant costumes, with historical rituals, dances, and processions that take place at Qorikancha, the Plaza de Armas, and the fortress of Sacsayhuamán.
inti-raymi.history: Originally established by the Inca Pachacuti in the 15th century, the festival marked the winter solstice and the start of the new year. It was banned by the Spanish in the 16th century but was revived in the 20th century as a theatrical event to honor Cusco's heritage.

traditions.tradition_4: Folkloric dances from the four suyus (regions) of the Inca Empire

schedule.event_1_desc: Ceremony begins at Qorikancha (Temple of the Sun).
schedule.event_2_desc: Procession moves to the Plaza de Armas for the "Encounter of the Times".
schedule.event_3_desc: Main ceremony at the esplanade of Sacsayhuamán.

corpus-christi.description: A massive religious procession where 15 saints and virgins parade through Cusco.
corpus-christi.longDescription: Corpus Christi in Cusco is a vibrant and unique syncretic festival, blending Catholic faith with ancient Andean traditions. Fifteen statues of saints and virgins from different parishes are carried in a grand procession to the Cusco Cathedral, where they 'visit' the body of Christ for eight days. The festival is famous for its elaborate decorations, music, and the traditional dish called Chiriuchu.
corpus-christi.history: Introduced by the Spanish in the 16th century, the festival was used to replace the Inca practice of parading ancestral mummies. The Andean people adapted the Catholic tradition, assigning their own sacred meanings to the saints, thus creating a powerful symbol of cultural resistance and fusion.

traditions.tradition_1: The entry of the 15 saints into the Plaza de Armas.
traditions.tradition_2: The consumption of 'Chiriuchu', a cold dish with various meats and ingredients.
traditions.tradition_4: The 'Octave of Corpus', where the saints return to their parishes a week later.

schedule.event_1_desc: Main procession of all saints and virgins around the Plaza de Armas.
schedule.event_2_desc: Gastronomic fairs in Plaza San Francisco to try Chiriuchu.
schedule.event_1_desc: Second procession as the saints return to their home parishes.

qoyllur-riti.description: A spiritual pilgrimage to the Sinakara Valley, blending Catholic and Andean beliefs.
qoyllur-riti.longDescription: Qoyllur Rit'i, or the "Snow Star Festival," is a centuries-old religious pilgrimage that takes place in the remote Sinakara Valley at the foot of Mount Ausangate. Tens of thousands of pilgrims from surrounding villages travel for days, bringing large crosses to the sanctuary. The festival is a unique syncretism of Catholic and Andean beliefs, celebrating the stars, the mountain spirits (Apus), and the Lord of Qoyllur Rit'i.
qoyllur-riti.history: The festival's origins are a blend of an 18th-century Catholic miracle story and ancient Andean mountain worship. It centers on the appearance of the Christ child to a young shepherd boy. It has been recognized by UNESCO as part of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

traditions.tradition_1: Night-long vigils with music and dance
traditions.tradition_2: Processions of "Ukukus" (bear-men dancers) to the glacier
traditions.tradition_3: Elaborate dance performances by different "nations" representing their communities
traditions.tradition_4: A final 24-hour procession for the Corpus Christi festival in Cusco

schedule.event_1_desc: Pilgrims arrive at Mahuayani, beginning the 8km walk to the sanctuary.
Main day of celebration with continuous music, dancing, and religious services.
"Serenata" concert for the Christ of Qoyllur Rit'i.
schedule.event_2_desc: Processions and farewell dances as pilgrims begin their journey home.

paucartambo-virgen-del-carmen.description: A vibrant and chaotic festival in the colonial town of Paucartambo with masked dancers.
paucartambo-virgen-del-carmen.longDescription: The festival in honor of the Virgen del Carmen is one of Peru's most celebrated and wild parties. For several days, the quiet colonial town of Paucartambo erupts in a riot of color, music, and dance. Troupes of masked dancers in spectacular costumes take over the streets, each representing different characters and stories from Peruvian history and folklore. The festival culminates in a procession where the statue of the Virgin blesses the town and battles costumed demons on the rooftops.
paucartambo-virgen-del-carmen.history: The devotion to the Virgen del Carmen (also known as Mamacha Carmen) dates back to the colonial era. Legend says her face miraculously appeared on a rock, and the festival grew around this veneration. The dances themselves are a syncretic mix of Catholic, Andean, and even Amazonian influences.

traditions.tradition_1: Parades of costumed dance troupes like Saqra (devils), Qhapaq Negro, and Maqta
traditions.tradition_4: The "burning" of the demons on the final day

schedule.event_1_desc: Fireworks and music mark the beginning of the festival.
schedule.event_2_desc: First appearance of the dance troupes in the main square.
schedule.event_1_desc: Main mass in honor of the Virgen del Carmen.
schedule.event_2_desc: Grand procession through the town streets with the statue of the Virgin.
schedule.event_1_desc: The battle between the angels and demons takes place, with demons performing acrobatics on the rooftops.

qeswachaka-bridge-festival.description: The annual reconstruction of the last Inca rope bridge.
qeswachaka-bridge-festival.longDescription: The Q'eswachaka Bridge Festival is an extraordinary example of living Inca heritage. Every year, four communities come together to rebuild this rope bridge using traditional techniques passed down for centuries. The four-day process is a communal ritual that involves ceremonies, work, and celebration, culminating in the crossing of the new bridge.
qeswachaka-bridge-festival.history: This tradition has been maintained for over 500 years, being a vital link for communication between communities. In 2013, the knowledge, techniques, and rituals associated with the reconstruction of the Q'eswachaka bridge were recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

traditions.tradition_4: Weaving and assembly of the new bridge by specialists.
traditions.tradition_5: Inaugural crossing with music and dance.

schedule.event_1_desc: Dismantling of the old ropes and weaving of the new ones.
schedule.event_2_desc: Assembly and installation of the new bridge.

linderaje-chinchero.description: Ritual combat to define communal boundaries.
linderaje-chinchero.longDescription: Linderaje is a ritual combat practice that takes place in Chinchero to settle land disputes between communities. Far from being a violent brawl, it is a regulated and symbolic confrontation that strengthens social ties and reaffirms territorial identity. It is a display of strength and community organization that ends with celebration, regardless of the outcome.
linderaje-chinchero.history: Of pre-Hispanic origin, these ritual battles were a way for communities to manage conflicts and demonstrate their vitality. The Spanish colonists tried to suppress them, but the tradition has endured, adapting over time and becoming a fundamental part of the local cultural calendar.

traditions.tradition_2: Use of traditional clothing and whips (warakas).
traditions.tradition_3: Presence of music and dance to encourage the fighters.
traditions.tradition_4: The fight ends with a communal agreement and celebration.

schedule.event_1_desc: The communities gather at the boundary lines to begin the ritual.
